positions.name: CalibrationVerifiedAgainstReferencePlates
positions.frame: how is the Kestrelwood spectrograph's calibration status established and verified?
positions.why: All three expressions ground the calibration claim in the same directional move: the instrument's status is settled not by assertion alone but by checking it against a fixed external standard — the June reference plates. src-1 states this narratively ('We verified the calibration against the June reference plates and it holds'), while src-2 and src-3 restate the same instrument/value pairing in structured field-label form ('Instrument: Kestrelwood spectrograph', 'Calibration: 88.4 MHz, verified against June reference plates'). The dimensional reads reinforce the coherence: all three sit in the technical/field-label register, calm-positive affect, present/realis/concrete temporal footing, authority-ranking relational stance toward the reference standard, and expert/informational power — a single verification-against-standard read spanning prose and structured restatement alike. No tension: narrative and log-line forms agree on the same fact and its warrant.
